headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. In this guide: Key election dates Check voter registration status How to register to vote How to find your polling place What to bring to your polling place How to track your mail-in ballot Why is California choosing a new governor? 14 California propositions What to watch Alameda County What to watch Contra Costa County What to watch Napa County What to watch San Francisco What to watch San Mateo County What to watch Santa Clara County What to watch Solano County County election offices Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot. Use the expandable graphic below for a breakdown on what to know about each measure. 2026 California Ballot Propositions Click on a proposition to see more information about what will happen if it does or doesn’t pass. Source: NBC Staff Reports • Interactive: Annetta Stogniew Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Contra Costa County In Contra Costa County, several county board of education seats are open. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Napa County California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. Measure B in Napa County: Sales tax to fund wildfire prevention and open space preservation. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Napa County and additional election information, visit the Napa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Francisco San Francisco voters will weigh in on several open seats on the county board of supervisors and board of education. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website. Races and measures to watch in Sonoma County California Congressional District 1: Mike McGuire will face James Gallagher in a seat redistricted by Proposition 50. California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. State Assembly District 12: Eric Lucan and Jackie Elward compete in a battle between business and labor. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Sonoma County and additional election information, visit the Sonoma County Registrar of Voters website. headlines.title: Watch live: Updates on deadly shooting at Monterey County's Moss Landing
headlines.description: Multiple people were killed in a shooting in the Monterey County community of Moss Landing early Monday morning, according to officials. The Monterey County Sheriff’s Office said the shooting happened just after midnight along Jetty Road, which runs between Moss Landing State Beach and Elkhorn Slough. Multiple fatalities and causalities were confirmed, the sheriff’s office said. There is no active threat to the Moss Landing community, according to the sheriff’s office. Authorities closed Jetty Road and Moss Landing State Beach. An investigation is underway. Additional information wasn’t immediately available. This is a developing news story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates.

headlines.title: Opening statements begin in retrial of Sierra LaMar murder case
headlines.description: A retrial for Antolin Garcia-Torres, the man once convicted in the murder of Morgan Hill teenager Sierra LaMar, kicked off Monday with opening statements. Earlier this year, an appeals court overturned the murder and kidnapping convictions for Garcia-Torres on grounds that prosecutors improperly consolidated three unrelated attempted kidnapping allegations from 2009 with the charge of murdering LaMar in 2012. LaMar, who was 15 years old at the time, disappeared from a Morgan Hill bus stop on her way to school. Her body has yet to be found. In 2017, a jury convicted Garcia-Torres of her murder, in part because of DNA evidence that connected him to the crime, but that conviction was later overturned, with the court ruling there was improper cross-admission of evidence by tying the attempted kidnappings to the murder charge. The court said that unfairly prejudiced Garcia-Torres. On Monday, the prosecution showed jurors the last selfie LaMar took and the last text she sent to a friend in the moments before she disappeared, a simple “ye” when her friend asked LaMar to bring her stuff. Jurors also saw a picture of LaMar’s red shoes that dogs used to try to pick up her scent in order to find her remains as well as a photo of her cellphone that was found ditched in a field by her home. The jury also heard the 911 call from LaMar’s mother in the hours after her disappearance. Legal analyst Steven Clark said the recording was not only haunting but effective for the prosecution. The prosecution is expected to wrap up its opening statement Monday afternoon. The defense, if it chooses, can deliver its own opening statement. Witness testimony is expected to begin Tuesday. headlines.title: Bay Area beaches face dangerous surf this week as light rain returns
headlines.description: Bay Area beachgoers are being warned to watch out for dangerous waves and strong ocean currents this week, with hazardous beach conditions expected through Tuesday evening and again Thursday through the weekend. In an advisory issued around 1:40 a.m. Monday, the National Weather Service said that long-period ocean swells will increase the risk of sneaker waves and strong rip currents along the Pacific Coast. The waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the ocean from beaches, jetties and rocks, forecasters said. The first period of hazardous beach conditions is expected to last through Tuesday evening. Another round is forecast from Thursday through Sunday. Waves could reach 13 to 17 feet Thursday through Sunday, according to the weather service. The forecast calls for a 15- to 17-second westerly or northwesterly swell, increasing the risk of dangerous surf. Beachgoers are urged to stay out of the water, avoid jetties, piers and rocks, and never turn their backs on the ocean. The weather service also expects light rain across much of the Bay Area on Tuesday. The interior Central Coast is expected to see little or no rain. Rainfall amounts are expected to vary by location. Temperatures, meanwhile, are expected to remain seasonal to slightly below seasonal through Thursday, the weather service said.

headlines.title: Fairfield community members grieve, call for change after Spirit store shooting
headlines.description: Some neighbors and community leaders came together in Fairfield Sunday night for a community vigil following Friday’s mass shooting inside a Spirit Halloween store. One woman, 31-year-old Constance Hages, was killed in the shooting. Her family members told police that she was pregnant. Six other people were injured. Sunday’s vigil, hosted by the Solano County organization Broken By Violence, was held to offer a safe space for people to grieve, pray, and process. News of Friday’s shooting felt especially close to home for many in the area who have shopped at the mall before or visited that very store to shop for Halloween costumes. “People don’t feel safe in our community,” said Joy Forte, president of Broken By Violence. “Just a simple going to get a Halloween costume or whatever, and people’s lives are lost, and people are impacted.” “Senseless,” she emphasized. Fairfield Oct 31 Fairfield Oct 30 The vigil partnered with local groups that provide resources, including Napa-Solano County SANE-SART, which provides forensic and mental health services. “One bullet moves through an entire community,” said Kari Cordero with SANE-SART. At the vigil, many people said they felt especially fearful or upset in light of several recent instances of gun violence in Solano County. On Halloween, Vallejo police said a man died after being shot. Also on Halloween, Vacaville police said a 15-year-old boy was shot and is currently recovering. “I’m tired of the pattern,” Cordero said. “Something terrible happens, we gather, we light candles, leaders step up to the microphone and say this isn’t going to happen again, and here we are yet again.” People at the vigil called for more funding for violence prevention efforts and staff, as well as more investment in community patrols. The Spirit store in Fairfield remained closed Sunday, with a small memorial growing outside the door. Fairfield police said Sunday that four of the six people who were injured in the shooting were still in the hospital. One of those people, a 19-year-old man, was in critical condition. Police have not made any arrests in the shooting or shared details about any potential suspects.

headlines.title: Person arrested after shooting across San Jose City Hall
headlines.description: A person was arrested after a shooting across San Jose City Hall on Sunday, according to police. Officers responded to a report of a firearm discharged on Santa Clara and 6th streets around 4:16 p.m., according to police. The reporting party had told police a person was shooting a firearm in the area. At the scene, officers found the suspect and arrested him around 4:20 p.m., according to officials. Police said nobody was hurt and the investigation is active and ongoing.

headlines.title: ‘Just overwhelming': Gabby Williams' childhood coach on Valkyries' historic win
headlines.description: Right after helping carry the Golden State Valkyries to their first-ever WNBA title on Saturday, star forward Gabby Williams hugged her former coach, Alfonso Joo. Gabby Williams was named WNBA Finals MVP. Joo was William’s youth coach in the Bay Area and has known her since she was a little girl. “Words can’t describe how much joy I had for her how proud I was it was just overwhelming,” Joo said. Joo has coached basketball for about 30 years and still runs the Bulldawgs program in San Francisco. He coached Williams during her middle school years, when she would frequent the Bay Area from Reno. “I have the opportunity to have coached Gabby, and I have a great relationship as being, I guess, her godfather, as she puts it,” he said. Golden State Valkyries 15 hours ago Golden State Valkyries Oct 31 Golden State Valkyries Nov 1 Joo is still on cloud nine from Saturday night, witnessing a former player rise all the way to the top. When the game was over, Joo moved towards the floor and Williams told security to wave them in. Joo said he told her, “This is what I’ve always wanted for you.” “She has to take something into the second the third fourth and fifth gear I didn’t think she had the sixth gear but apparently she does,” he said. “And she led by example.” It’s also what Joo says Williams has wanted for herself: to play among the greatest. And she showed she deserves to be right there with the best of them – now inspiring the future. “I mean when you get a kid that does not go out trick or treating to watch the game just to watch the game that tells you a lot,” Joo said. “They’re sending you photos of them holding the ball, they’re shooting at night time wearing her jersey, I’ve got pictures of them wearing her jersey are they inspired yeah, yeah.”

headlines.title: Gabby Williams hugs youth coach after leading Valkyries to victory
headlines.description: A big part of Saturday’s win for the Valkyries was thanks to Forward Gabby Williams, who showed up big in the third quarter. Williams scored 30 points in the game and was named WNBA Finals MVP. This after arriving as a free agent before the season. While Williams is from Reno, she has extended family in the Bay Area and visited frequently as a kid, even playing for Alfonzo Joo in the Bulldawgs Basketball Club, a youth organization in San Francisco. Joo told NBC Bay Area the two have remained close throughout Williams’ career. They were seen hugging after Saturday’s game on the court, right after it was called. Joo has coached basketball for about 30 years and still runs the Bulldawgs program.

headlines.title: 15-year-old injured after Halloween shooting in Vacaville
headlines.description: A 15-year-old was hurt following a shooting in Vacaville on Halloween night, according to the Vacaville Police Department. Officers responded to a shooting outside a home near Canterbury Circle and Hampton Street at 10:22 p.m., the police department said. There, authorities said they found a 15-year-old lying on the roadway who appeared to have been shot. The teenager was taken to the hospital in critical condition, according to police. Authorities later said the teen is in stable condition and expected to survive. Preliminary information suggests this was an isolated incident stemming from an argument during a gathering at a nearby home, officials said. They said the suspect is still at large and has not been identified. The police department encourages anyone with information to contact its anonymous tip line at 707-454-5722.

headlines.title: Thousands celebrate Día de los Muertos in the Bay Area
headlines.description: On Sunday, thousands of people celebrated Día de los Muertos with events in the Bay Area. In Oakland, tens of thousands of people came out to the Fruitvale neighborhood for one of city’s largest Día de los Muertos celebrations. The free, family-friendly festival featured live music, traditional altars, Latin American artisans, performances, a low rider show, and activities for all ages. The theme this year was “La Lucha Continúa: Aquí Estamos Y No Nos Vamos” (the struggle continues: we are here and we’re not leaving). The Children’s Discovery Museum in San Jose also held its Día de los Muertos celebration, with an event that encouraged families with children to honor departed loved ones and learn more about Mexican culture. The celebration included traditional Aztec dancing, “calacas processions” of giant skeleton puppets and a special stop at “Lupe,” the museum’s 14,000-year-old mammoth. Craft stations were also set up for the children. Sunday’s program at the Children’s Museum was made possible in part by a “Cultural Affairs grant” from the city of San Jose.

headlines.title: Valkyries win WNBA championship in second season, beating Dream 68-63 in Game 7
headlines.description: Gabby Williams scored her team’s final 11 points of the third quarter and dazzled through the fourth on the way to 30 points, and the Golden State Valkyries captured a championship in just their second season by beating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in a sensational first WNBA Finals Game 7 on Saturday night. Jordin Canada scored 18 points, Allisha Gray 16 and Angel Reese had eight points and 12 rebounds for the Dream, denied another championship in the franchise’s fourth try. Gray made two free throws with 11 seconds left then Atlanta forced a jump ball — Gray against Williams — and Veronica Burton corralled it and converted two free throws with 5.1 seconds to go. “I’m just so blessed, this is insane!” said Burton, cut by Dallas two years ago. Rhyne Howard’s layup tied it at 57 with 2:41 left only for Williams to answer once more with a clutch 3-pointer. She converted two free throws with 1:40 remaining, then Kiah Stokes scored a late basket. Stokes pulled down 13 rebounds and blocked two more shots to cap her spectacular postseason. Williams left Seattle with a great feeling about joining Golden State and its close-knit culture, returning to the Bay Area where she played youth basketball to build something special with the Valkyries — and she’s now done that. Fans chanted “Gabby! Gabby!” throughout the fourth quarter. “All it took was good people,” she said. “All we heard last year was we don’t have no stars. We don’t have no talent. Yeah right! We got good people. We got good people. We got winners. We got people who are ready to put their bodies on the floor to win a game.” When the final buzzer sounded, the violet-clad sellout crowd at Chase Center went into a frenzy as players sprinted onto the floor to hug and celebrate as confetti fell from the rafters. “Ballhalla” had become “Boohalla” for this far-but-haunted Halloween night in the raucous arena. Now, with a women’s championship to its name right alongside the one earned by the Golden State Warriors in 2022. “We gotta build a bigger trophy case,” co-owner Peter Guber said. The team that led at halftime in the first six matchups had won every game so far, and the Dream were ahead 30-24 at the break. Atlanta also had been 16-0 this season when Reese made at least one 3. The Dream’s DeWanna Bonner became the first player in WNBA history to reach 600 career postseason defensive rebounds. Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase changed her starting lineup in a move that paid huge dividends after Golden State fell behind 2-1, inserting Kaila Charles and Tiffany Hayes and bringing Kayla Thornton and Cecilia Zandalasini off the bench. The 37-year-old Hayes, who came out of retirement two years ago and spent 10 seasons with the Dream, scored 11 points in the winner-take-all Game 7 and brought energy all series that made Nakase want to win for the veteran guard as much as anybody. Valkyries owner Joe Lacob guaranteed a championship within the first five years for this franchise three years ago when the Bay Area was granted an expansion team, and in improbable, joyful fashion, his team accomplished it in Year 2. That after becoming the first expansion organization to reach the playoffs in its inaugural year in 2025. During the victory ceremony, Lacob shouted out the team and its leaders, while Nakase, general manager Ohemma Nyanin and President Jess Smith hugged. And Lacob thanked the fans who have sold out Chase Center for every game since Day 1. “Ballhalla!” Lacob hollered. WNBA Oct 30 Golden State Valkyries Oct 30 Nakase and Valkyries are determined to avoid another slow start in WNBA Finals Game 7 against Dream

headlines.title: Pregnant woman killed in shooting that left other 6 hurt at Halloween store in Fairfield
headlines.description: A pregnant woman was killed in a shooting that left other six people hurt inside the Spirit Halloween store at the Solano Town Center in Fairfield on Friday night, police said Saturday. Police identified the victim as 31-year-old Constance Hages. Authorities said Hages’ family told detectives she was pregnant at the time of her death, but police said the information will be confirmed following an examination by the Solano County Coroner. Fairfield police said it is believed the shooting stemmed from a “targeted incident” involving one suspect inside the Spirit Halloween Store. On Friday, officers responded to a shooting inside the Solano Town Center at the Spirit Halloween store at 8:30 p.m., according to authorities. Seven people were shot and one of them died. Authorities reported that the victims who remain in critical condition are a 16-year-old boy, a 19-year-old man and a 32-year-old man. Officials said a 23-year-old man remains hospitalized “in critical but stable condition,” while a 19-year-old man and a 43-year-old man received treatment for gunshot wounds and have since been released from the hospital. “Fairfield’s greatest strength is how we all look out for each other. I urge everyone in our community to support one another in this obviously very troubled time, especially now,” Fairfield Mayor Rick Vaccaro said on Saturday. “Obviously, it’s going to be on everybody’s mind when an incident like this occurs, and I know it will always be on my mind for a long time.” Spirit Halloween released a statement regarding the shooting: “We are deeply saddened by the tragic incident that occurred inside of the Solano Town Center at the Spirit Halloween store in Fairfield, CA. Our thoughts and prayers are with the families of the victims of this heartbreaking incident. We are fully cooperating with local law enforcement as they investigate the circumstances surrounding this event. As this remains an active investigation, we defer to the Fairfield Police Department for further details. Out of respect for those impacted and to support the ongoing investigation, the store will remain closed until further notice.” Solano Town Center’s planned Halloween trick-or-treating event was cancelled following the incident, according to the mall’s website. Fairfield police said this is an ongoing investigation. They ask anyone with information to contact them at 707-428-7600 or email 1030mall@fairfield.ca.gov.
